title: Zagreb Čistoća workers protest over proposed dismissals and working conditions
location: Outside the Čistoća company building, Zagreb
organizer: Čistoća workers; no formal organizer identified in the opened reports
participants_original: HRT described several hundred workers demonstrating outside the company building on 24 January. RFE/RL reported 1,000 employees in the protest without specifying whether that was a simultaneous turnout or cumulative count.
threshold_50_evidence: HRT’s opened 24 January report describes several hundred workers demonstrating outside the company building, which qualitatively establishes at least 50 at that reported gathering; no exact bounds are inferred. RFE/RL’s 1,000 employees lacks a counting method and site/time scope.

title.summary: RFE/RL and HRT report a Zagreb Čistoća workers’ protest/strike over three proposed dismissals and additional workplace demands.

start_date.summary: RFE/RL says the protest began Monday 23 January; HRT also says the work stoppage began the previous day, 23 January.

end_date.summary: RFE/RL reports that on 26 January worker representatives and the mayor reached an agreement, workers said the strike had ended and returned to waste collection, and the protest had lasted four days. HRT’s 24 January report alone does not establish an endpoint.

location.summary: HRT places several hundred workers demonstrating outside the Čistoća company building; RFE/RL identifies the company as a Zagreb city public enterprise.

scope.summary: Both opened reports concern one local Zagreb public-employer dispute. The physical demonstration is observed at the company building; later activity is described as a strike.

organizer.summary: Reports describe workers initiating the action; no union or formal organizer is identified as leading this gathering.

demands.summary: HRT lists a 12% base-pay increase, permanent supplement, higher job coefficients, protective equipment and free parking; RFE/RL reports wages and workplace rights alongside opposition to three planned dismissals.

participants_original.summary: HRT says several hundred demonstrated outside the building on 24 January; RFE/RL says 1,000 employees were in the protest but gives no count method or simultaneity scope.

participants_min.summary: No numeric lower bound is derived from qualitative attendance or the ambiguous employee total.

participants_max.summary: No numeric upper bound is supported.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: HRT’s qualitative “several hundred” attendance description establishes the 50-person threshold for the outside-company-building demonstration; no interval is inferred.

protester_violence.summary: Neither report establishes protester violence or an explicit absence; code unknown.

state_response.summary: RFE/RL reports a direct meeting with the mayor and an agreement to meet five of eleven demands immediately and negotiate six more; other response dimensions are not established.

state_response.accommodation.summary: The mayor met worker representatives and reached a partial agreement; this is accommodation evidence, not proof of a full victory.

eligibility.summary: Pending state-target review because the employer is a city-owned company and the mayor negotiated the agreement; assess whether this local public-authority target qualifies under the original Mass Mobilization rules.

notes: The public assembly is specifically evidenced on 24 January outside the company building. Reports frame a broader 23–26 January protest/strike episode; the exact boundary between assembly days and workplace stoppage is not fully resolved. HRT lists labor demands; RFE/RL reports the mayoral agreement and return to work. HRT credits HRT, HINA and multiple desks; do not treat it as independent from HINA-origin coverage without a written-origin check.
open_questions: Review local city-owned public-company targeting against the original codebook and unavailable official baseline.
Clarify whether the 23–26 January episode should be represented as one continuous protest/strike or the Jan 24 public gathering nested in a work stoppage.
The 1,000 employee figure has no counting method; retain qualitative HRT attendance and do not use the total as a range.
